title: First Halting Time of the Evaluator
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Boolean Turing machine, and let $w$, $s$, and $o$ be Boolean words. If $M$ halts on input $s$ with output $o$ after $T$ steps, then there are $t\le T$ and a Boolean boundary tag $b$ such that at time $t$ the run of $M$ is halted with output $o$, and $b$ correctly marks the boundary of its input-head position. At every earlier time $j<t$, the capture-wrapped evaluator started from the configuration prepared using physical input $w$ and the initial configuration of $M$ on $s$ has not reached its return state; at time $t$ its configuration is exactly the evaluator configuration associated with the time-$t$ configuration of $M$ and tag $b$.
hypotheses_covered: M is a finite-state Boolean Turing machine
w, s, and o are Boolean words
M computes output o on s within time T
replaced:
Let $M$ compute output $o$ on argument $s$ within time $T$. Then there is a time $t \le
T$ and a boundary tag such that the run of $M$ from its initial configuration on $s$ is
halted at $t$ with output $o$, the capture-wrapped evaluator started on the prepared
candidate does not visit its return state before $t$, and at time $t$ it is exactly the
evaluator configuration of that halted run.
